standard_prerequisites.name: Assumptions of the general gap theorem
standard_prerequisites.statement: A family of coordinate transition matrices whose parameters satisfy the spectral independence bounds of the general theorem.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are inherited by the corollary.

standard_prerequisites.name: Uniform gap parameter
standard_prerequisites.statement: The parameter delta entering the general gap theorem bounds the spectral gap of every coordinate step.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the quantity appearing in the contraction rate.

standard_prerequisites.name: Operator norm of the product
standard_prerequisites.statement: The norm of the product of the coordinate matrices measured on mean-zero functions.

core_obligations: Check that the assumptions of the general gap theorem are satisfied in the systematic scan case, where the parameters k_j are simply the indices j (source line 543).
Apply that theorem and read off the contraction rate with the factor eight times n plus one appearing in the denominator (source line 543).

proof_roadmap.step: Verify the assumptions for the systematic scan.
Apply the general gap theorem and read the rate.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled corollary at source lines 535-541: under the assumptions of the general spectral gap theorem, the operator norm of the product of the coordinate matrices is at most one minus delta over eight times n plus one. The proof (source lines 542-548) is short, but it does two things the statement hides: it has to check that the parameter choice of the systematic scan, namely k_j equal to j for every coordinate, satisfies the hypotheses of the general theorem, and then it instantiates that theorem, which is where the explicit rate with the denominator eight times n plus one comes from. The statement records only the contraction bound.
